actions.blurb: A studio is your program: a roster, the work you assign, and a join code you give out once. Everything else in IPT hangs off it.
actions.name: createStudio
actions.title: Starting a studio

actions.blurb: A performer enters the code their instructor gave them and lands in the studio with this week's work already on screen. There is nothing else to set up.
actions.name: joinStudio
actions.title: Joining a studio

actions.blurb: Assign a piece with a weekly target and the instructions you would give in the room: hands separate, take it at 72, sticking as written. They have it on Tuesday night when you are not there.
actions.name: assignWork
actions.title: Assigning the work

actions.blurb: A performer starts a session before they play and stops it when they are done, so the time is counted rather than remembered. Sessions are saved on the phone first, so a practice room with no signal never loses one.
actions.name: logPractice
actions.title: Logging a session

actions.blurb: The performer plays their own click out loud and the take catches both, so their instructor can hear how the two line up. They mark the moments worth hearing, which turns a four-minute recording into a ten-second listen.
actions.name: recordTake
actions.title: Recording a take

actions.blurb: Each instruction on the plan gets ticked off as it is worked. It is deliberately worth no points, because a self-report you pay for stops being information.
actions.name: markFocusPoint
actions.title: Ticking off the plan

actions.blurb: You hear a take and send one line back. This is the step every rival product is missing, and a performer who thinks nobody listens stops recording inside a fortnight.
actions.name: acknowledgeSession
actions.title: Saying you heard it

actions.blurb: One line to one performer, with no thread and no reply. It reaches somebody who has gone quiet without turning the app into a chat client.
actions.name: sendNudge
actions.title: Sending one line

actions.blurb: Promote an assistant to instructor, move somebody between sections, or remove a performer who has left. A second adult in the room is the normal case, not the edge one.
actions.name: manageRoster
actions.title: Running the roster

actions.blurb: Tune what earns points, or switch the leaderboard off entirely. Running a studio without one is a first-class choice. What cannot be done is letting raw minutes outscore finishing the work.
actions.name: setScoring
actions.title: How the studio scores

actions.blurb: Tell IPT when your program is in session, so summer and exam weeks do not read as weeks somebody failed to practice. A break is not a miss.
actions.name: setTerms
actions.title: When the studio is running

actions.blurb: A performer's name, instrument and color are what the studio sees beside their practice. There are no photographs anywhere in IPT, and that is deliberate.
actions.name: editProfile
actions.title: Your profile

actions.blurb: An account carries your studios, your practice and your recordings, on every device you sign in on. The demo needs none of it, which is why it is open to anybody.
actions.name: createAccount
actions.title: Your own account

actions.blurb: A real account can be deleted from inside the app, and IPT names what that destroys before it happens: the studios, the people and the hours. The demo has no account to delete.
actions.name: deleteAccount
actions.title: Deleting an account

instructor.body: Set a weekly time target for one performer or the whole studio, and add your notes on what to work on: hands separate, take it at 72, fix the release in bar 12. Your notes are on the screen while they practice, so nobody has to remember them from rehearsal.
instructor.title: Assign the week's work

instructor.body: A performer can attach a short recording to a session. They play their own metronome out loud, so the take catches the playing and the click together, and they can flag the moments they want you to hear. You can turn recording off for the whole studio.
instructor.title: Hear how it went

instructor.body: Your dashboard lists the performers who are behind before the ones who are fine. Open somebody's week, listen to what they sent, and write a line back.
instructor.title: See who needs you first

instructorQuestions.answer: Everything you assigned that week, finished. Time rounds down, so 44 minutes of a 45-minute target is not met. IPT never credits a minute somebody did not practice.
instructorQuestions.question: What counts as a week being met?

instructorQuestions.answer: A week you assigned nothing in is not a week anybody failed. If your program has real breaks, set them under Terms, and weeks outside a term stop counting against anybody. Without that, a summer off would end every streak in the studio.
instructorQuestions.question: Why did somebody's streak not break over the holidays?

instructorQuestions.answer: Yes, and the performer can flag the moments they want you to hear. Listen to all plays the queue one recording at a time, taking one from each performer before anybody's second.
instructorQuestions.question: Can I see how long a recording is before I play it?

instructorQuestions.answer: Practice is saved on their own device before it is sent, so a room with no signal does not lose it. It appears for you when their app next has a connection. If a session says it could not be added to the studio, the assignment it belonged to was probably deleted.
instructorQuestions.question: A performer's practice isn't showing up.

instructorQuestions.answer: Settings → Scoring → No points. The standings disappear rather than sitting there empty, and assignments, practice and recordings work exactly the same. Plenty of programs run well without a leaderboard.
instructorQuestions.question: Can I turn the points off?

performer.body: Stop it when you are done and IPT keeps the time for you. What your instructor asked for is on the screen the whole time, so you are not working from memory. If you forget to start one, you can write the session down afterward.
performer.title: Start a session before you play

performer.body: It is optional, and it is the part your instructor can answer. Play your metronome out loud and the take catches both. Mark this spot flags a moment while you are recording, so they go straight to the bit you meant.
performer.title: Add a recording if you want to

performer.body: They listen to what you send and can write back. Nobody else in the studio can hear your recordings or read your notes. They see that you practiced, and for how long.
performer.title: Your instructor hears it

performerQuestions.answer: Your instructors, and nobody else. The rest of the studio can see that you practiced and for how long, but never your recordings, and never the notes you write.
performerQuestions.question: Who can hear my recordings?

performerQuestions.answer: Anything under two minutes is not counted, and IPT tells you when that happens, so a start you did not mean does not become a session you did not practice. Any real run at something clears two minutes.
performerQuestions.question: Does a really short session count?

performerQuestions.answer: It is safe. Sessions are saved on this device before they go anywhere, so nothing is lost in a room with no signal. It goes out by itself the next time you have a connection.
performerQuestions.question: My practice says it is waiting to send.

performerQuestions.answer: Minutes always round down, so 44 minutes of a 45-minute target is not met. It works the same way for everybody in the studio.
performerQuestions.question: Why did my time round down?

performerQuestions.answer: No. A session counts without one. A recording is what lets your instructor hear how it sounded and write back about it, which they cannot do from a number.
performerQuestions.question: Do I have to record something?
